quirks.title: The radio enforces its bands
quirks.text: The radio module itself only tunes 136.000 to 174.000 and 400.000 to 480.000 MHz. A frequency outside those is refused and the radio stays on the frequency it was on, so there is no 220 MHz or other out-of-band receive.

quirks.title: Packet data needs a long start
quirks.text: The transmitter needs about 1.5 seconds after keying before data comes through cleanly. A packet sent right at key-up is lost. SignalDeck therefore leads every APRS or packet transmission with 1.6 seconds of standard AX.25 flags and sends the frame twice.

quirks.title: Wait after changing channel before you talk
quirks.text: A channel change finishes inside the radio about 3 seconds after it is sent, and it stops a transmission that is already running. SignalDeck waits about 4 seconds after a retune before its own automatic transmissions; when you change channel by hand, wait a moment before you press Talk.

quirks.title: Signal readings lag a retune
quirks.text: Right after a frequency change the signal reading is 15 to 20 dB too low for about 0.7 seconds. That is why the band scope takes about 0.7 seconds per step (2 m in 25 kHz steps is about 2 minutes).

quirks.title: Squelch levels act as one
quirks.text: The radio's squelch levels 1 to 9 all behave like one threshold near -90 dBm. For anything finer, use SignalDeck's Soft SQ, which listens to the audio itself.

quirks.title: Transmitting can reset the USB cable
quirks.text: On some 2 m frequencies at high power, the radio's own signal gets into the phone's USB cable and resets the connection (wired Android Auto drops and reconnects after you let go). Other frequencies on the same band and UHF were fine. It is RF pickup, not an app fault: a ferrite choke, a shorter shielded cable, low power on that channel or wireless Android Auto help. SignalDeck notices when it happens and suggests these.

quirks.title: Use wide on VHF
quirks.text: Setting a VHF channel to narrow made the receiver deaf on our test unit, and only a phone reboot brought it back. SignalDeck's built-in VHF channels (APRS, SSTV, weather) use wide. On UHF both settings receive.

quirks.title: Talkgroups you hear
quirks.text: On a DMR channel the radio only passes group calls for the talkgroups in that channel's receive list, which holds up to 32. Private calls to your own DMR ID always come through.

quirks.title: Receive audio is telephone-quality
quirks.text: The radio delivers its audio at 8 kHz and removes almost everything below about 250 Hz. Voice is fine; digital modes that need the low tones, such as M17, are decoded through a calibrated equalizer.

quirks.title: Long transmissions
quirks.text: SignalDeck releases the transmitter after 28 seconds of talk. A long high-power transmission warms the phone noticeably, and SignalDeck's heat guard stops long transmissions when the phone gets too hot.

measured.note: Requested offsets of 500 Hz to 5 kHz landed within 2 Hz of the target (2026-10-22), so Doppler correction in 500 Hz steps is real.

measured.what: Signal reading settle time after a retune
measured.note: Readings taken earlier were 15 to 20 dB low (2026-10-22).
Tone, flags and silence decoded alike at 1.6 s; shorter lost packets (2026-10-20).

measured.note: Back to normal in about 17 minutes (2026-10-25).

firmware.modified: SignalDeck module images from the signed firmware catalogue (Device, Radio firmware)
firmware.note: A loaded image stays in the module's flash across reboots. Loading the factory image again restores the stock firmware.

sections.head: Custom ROMs
sections.text: On a custom ROM or GSI the vendor radio audio service is usually missing. SignalDeck notices and takes the radio audio straight from the phone's sound card instead.

quirks.title: UHF only
quirks.text: The radio covers 400 to 480 MHz. There is no 2 m, no NOAA weather radio and no 2 m satellites.

quirks.title: No USB data while the radio is on
quirks.text: The radio is a USB device on the phone's only USB controller. While SignalDeck has the radio on, a computer cannot use the USB cable for data (adb, file transfer). Exit and Hand back switch the radio off and give the USB port back. Developers work over Wi-Fi ADB.

quirks.title: The signal meter pauses during a reception
quirks.text: Any command sent across the USB bridge while audio streams can break the audio. So during a reception the S-meter shows the reading from just before it and moves again when the reception ends. Fox hunt and coverage logging still take readings, which may cost a short drop-out.

quirks.title: A nearby transmitter deafens it
quirks.text: Another radio keying close by, even on a different UHF frequency, pushes this receiver down to the bottom of its range for the length of that key. It recovers at once when the other radio stops, and it does not fake a reception.

quirks.title: The reception signal can stick
quirks.text: Rarely, the bridge's reception start and end signal stops for a whole session. SignalDeck notices, finds receptions from the signal reading instead and restarts the bridge once; a phone reboot always clears it.

quirks.title: Short audio drop-outs
quirks.text: The bridge's USB audio can stop for about 2 seconds. SignalDeck restarts the bridge, which costs a few seconds without sound.

quirks.title: Switch off App block
quirks.text: The phone's App block setting force-stops SignalDeck 5 minutes after the screen goes off. SignalDeck opens that settings page once so you can switch it off for SignalDeck.

quirks.title: Charger noise
quirks.text: With a charger on the USB socket the idle signal reading rises by a few dB. Reception detection copes with it.

measured.value: -101 to -103 dBm, about -98 dBm with a charger
measured.note: Test unit, 2026-10-29.

quirks.title: FM only, 400 to 470 MHz
quirks.text: There is no DMR in this radio, so the DMR pages, contacts and messages are hidden. 2 m modes such as APRS monitoring on 144.390 and NOAA weather are out of band.

quirks.title: No signal meter
quirks.text: The module answers no signal-strength query. The meter shows RECEIVING or QUIET from the radio's receive line, and tools that need readings (band scope, fox hunting, coverage maps) are limited or hidden.

quirks.title: Low tones are cut hard
quirks.text: The receiver removes almost everything below about 300 Hz, more steeply than the Armor. Voice is fine; M17 receive uses its own calibration for it.

quirks.title: SignalDeck plays the audio
quirks.text: The module's own speaker route stays off at a fixed volume and SignalDeck plays the radio audio itself, so the phone's volume keys work as usual. There is a slight delay.

quirks.title: DCS codes
quirks.text: DCS tone squelch works with normal-polarity codes only.

quirks.title: Small screen
quirks.text: The screen is 480 by 854. SignalDeck uses a compact intercom layout here.

quirks.title: Its speaker stays on while it sends data
quirks.text: SignalDeck's own sounds (APRS, tones, SSTV, FT8) go through a relay to the radio, and the phone's speaker amplifier cannot be switched off for that moment, so the tones can be heard from the phone while it transmits them.

quirks.title: Mains chargers put a buzz on the air
quirks.text: With the phone on a mains charger, a 120 Hz buzz got into its transmitted and received audio in a test with two of these phones; data modes that tolerate noise (RTTY, FT8, APRS) still decoded, DTMF and PSK31 did not. On battery, or on a clean charger, it is gone.

measured.note: -57 dB at 125 to 187 Hz (HackRF test transmissions).
Over the air, with this phone's calibration.

firmware.note: The stock app carries no module firmware file and the module has no read command.

quirks.title: UHF only
quirks.text: Despite "dual band" in some listings, the radio answers only 400 to 480 MHz; VHF frequencies are never acknowledged.

quirks.title: The app's own sounds go through a gateway relay
quirks.text: Your voice goes from the microphone straight to the radio. Sounds SignalDeck makes itself (APRS, Morse ID, tones, SSTV, FT8) go through the relay the stock app uses for its network gateway, which feeds the phone's audio to the radio's microphone input while it transmits. It is a voice path: nothing below about 300 Hz and a cut above 3 kHz, so M17 cannot be sent.

quirks.title: Transmit frequency runs high
quirks.text: Our test unit transmitted about 1.6 kHz above the set frequency on FM and DMR alike, measured against a test receiver whose own error is part of that figure. It is inside what most DMR radios accept, but a narrow or strict receiver, or a DMR hotspot, may need its receive offset adjusted or may show a high bit error rate for this radio.

quirks.title: DMR voice audio is quiet
quirks.text: DMR calls are detected with the caller's ID, but the decoded voice reaches the app far below FM audio. This is under investigation.

quirks.title: Its transmitter desensitises nearby radios
quirks.text: While it keys, a radio close by on another UHF frequency hears less (its signal reading drops), though it does not open.

quirks.title: Mains chargers put a buzz on the air
quirks.text: With the phone on a mains charger, a 120 Hz buzz got into its transmitted and received audio in a test with two of these phones; data modes that tolerate noise (RTTY, FT8, APRS) still decoded, DTMF and PSK31 did not. On battery, or on a clean charger, it is gone.

measured.note: +1598, +1575 and +1604 Hz on three keys (2026-10-29). Includes the test receiver's own error: the same receiver reads an Armor 26 Ultra +0.8 to 1.0 kHz high, so this radio alone is probably 0.6 to 0.8 kHz (about 1.5 ppm) high. Measured on one test unit; your radio may differ.

quirks.title: Untested profile
quirks.text: This profile comes from an owner's device report and the phone's stock app. It has not run on the phone yet, so SignalDeck does not take over the radio by itself, and it transmits only in the guided Transmit test session (Device, Device report). Owners can help with Device, Run all checks, then that session.

quirks.title: Looks like an Armor 26 Ultra
quirks.text: The phone has the same radio control nodes as the Armor 26 Ultra but its module is on another port. SignalDeck recognises it by its model name.

quirks.title: Driven as its own app does
quirks.text: Its stock walkie-talkie app is an older build than the Armor 26 Ultra's, with the same commands but fewer of them. SignalDeck follows it on this phone: a shorter start-up exchange with the module, the audio opened 0.6 s before the transmitter is keyed, no new key within 2 s of the last one, and its channel files for Import from the stock app. Whether the module answers the extra commands SignalDeck uses (signal strength, caller ID, monitor) is what Run all checks finds out.

quirks.title: Bands not measured
quirks.text: The bands shown are the Armor family's; this model's limits have not been measured yet.

firmware.note: SignalDeck does not load module firmware on this phone: its stock app has no update path and carries no module image.

quirks.title: Profile in testing
quirks.text: Testers have receive, MON, CTCSS and channel import working. Transmit stays blocked until the profile is verified, and SignalDeck does not take over the radio by itself.

quirks.title: Channel changes need a pause
quirks.text: The stock app never writes channels less than 1 second apart; a burst of quick changes made the module refuse MON. SignalDeck keeps the same gap and only sends the newest channel.

quirks.title: The module can stop taking commands
quirks.text: After an update the module was sometimes left on but not answering. SignalDeck checks at start-up and restarts the module when it does not answer.

quirks.title: Slower reception reports
quirks.text: The radio reports a reception later than the Armor, so scanning waits 2.5 seconds per channel.

quirks.title: Squelch after MON
quirks.text: On firmware V016 the squelch was seen to stay open after MON was switched off. SignalDeck now sends the channel, monitor and squelch in the stock app's order; tell us if it still happens.

quirks.title: Nothing is changed
quirks.text: Until a profile exists for this phone, SignalDeck does not power, tune or key the radio. Device, Run all checks collects what a profile needs; send the result so the radio can be supported and described here.
